title: SLO Pulseboard and Initiative Health Tether
creator: Marta Ruiz
description: Create a lightweight "Pulseboard" that continuously maps SLI attainment, error-budget runway, and initiative health into a single view so PMs and SREs can make fast prioritization decisions. The Pulseboard will surface near-term risks (<=72h runway), show per-initiative SLI deltas vs. targets, and provide a recommended action (throttle rollout / pause experiment / open incident). This ticket covers the product definition, acceptance criteria, data wiring, and the first MVP dashboard + rollout playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Pulseboard displays per-service SLI, target, and 7d trend for availability and p99 latency
Error-budget runway calculation is shown as hours and color-coded (green/yellow/red) with threshold tuning
Initiatives can be linked to services and show combined SLO impact and current burn rate
A lightweight ‘Recommended Action’ engine produces one of: No Action / Alert PM / Throttle Canary / Pause Rollout
Dashboard rows and recommended actions are filterable by team, region, and deployment tier
First rollout playbook (Oncall + PM + Eng) published with checklist and rollback thresholds
tasks: Define data model for initiative <-> service mapping and error-budget attribution
Schema work: extend telemetry pipeline to emit initiative_id on sampled traces and metrics
Build Grafana/Console Pulseboard panel and wire to SLO time-series endpoints
Implement simple ruleset for Recommended Action (config-driven thresholds) in backend
Draft and review rollout playbook with SRE and PM partners
QA: inject simulated burn scenarios and validate dashboard and playbook responses
Ship MVP and run 2-week pilot with Platform and Growth teams
notes: Trade-offs: MVP will not include automated throttling actions — only recommended actions — to reduce blast radius and speed delivery.
We intentionally use a conservative window (72h runway) for recommendations to avoid chasing transient noise.
We will attribute error-budget burn to initiatives using weighted service-importance when a service maps to multiple initiatives (configurable weights).
Longer-term: consider integrating regression-alerting tied to canonical prompt/eval sets per initiative (post-MVP).
